title: Flag reading criteria that conflict with defaults or landing invariants
summary: Add a check in the reading path so that, before a reading is accepted, each acceptance criterion is compared with the recorded defaults and the landing invariants. It flags a criterion that would fail work a default requires, or would allow an outcome an invariant forbids. The audience is the user who accepts readings and the verifier. Tests cover the two named cases: a criterion forbidding CHANGELOG.md while the changelog default applies, and a criterion allowing extra commits after the landing commit.

defaults_applied.how: A change reading lists CHANGELOG.md as a deliverable, and the criteria must not forbid it.
New unit tests cover the flagged and unflagged cases, and cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria require running the tests that show the flags happen.
The check is enforced in code rather than prose.
One focused check in the reading path.
The verifier runs cargo test for the new tests.
The criteria check that bad criteria are caught, not that code exists.

assumptions: Flagging means recording a visible finding on the reading, such as a warning shown with the proposal and stored in it. It does not silently rewrite criteria or hard-fail the reading.

The check is deterministic Rust in athena-core next to ensure_changelog in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs. It uses text matching on criteria plus the reading's defaults_applied and deliverables. An LLM judge is not used.

The changelog default is the one ensure_changelog adds (id 'changelog', CHANGELOG.md listed as a change deliverable). Other defaults from defaults.toml and records/default-expectations can be matched by a small table of rules, starting with the changelog rule.

The landing invariant is D55 in docs/decisions.md: a landing is one commit carrying the whole job, and no later commit is part of the job. A criterion that permits additional or follow-up commits after the landing commit is flagged.
No change to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows is needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A unit test shows a change reading whose criterion forbids touching CHANGELOG.md (for example 'CHANGELOG.md must not be modified') while the changelog default applies is flagged. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`.

A unit test shows a criterion that allows extra commits after the landing commit (for example 'follow-up commits may be added after landing') is flagged as allowing an outcome the landing invariant forbids. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`.
Negative tests show an ordinary criterion, and one that requires a CHANGELOG.md entry or exactly one landing commit, is not flagged. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`.

The flag names the offending criterion and the default or invariant it conflicts with, and is shown to the user with the proposal and stored on the reading. A user reading the proposal can see why it was flagged.

The check runs in the reading build path (build_reading, and correct if it rebuilds readings), so every change reading is checked before it is accepted. A study or declined reading is not flagged by the changelog rule.
`cargo test` passes for the workspace, `cargo clippy` is clean, and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

out_of_scope: Changing defaults.toml, athena.toml or any workflow file.
Changing the landing gate or its invariants themselves.
Using an LLM to judge criteria.
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower acceptance than the reference. The request leaves open what flagging does and how invariants are matched, and the work adds a new check plus tests across the reading path.
hard_reason: It touches the reading gate that judges other jobs' criteria, and it encodes the landing invariants, so a mistake would pass or block other jobs.
